content: Rabeprazole is a medication prescribed to treat conditions where the stomach produces excessive acid. These conditions include ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. Additionally, rabeprazole is used in combination with other medications to eradicate Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori), a bacterium responsible for causing ulcers. Rabeprazole belongs to a class of drugs known as proton-pump inhibitors (PPIs), which function by reducing the production of stomach acid. Rabeprazole is available as a delayed-release tablet, designed for oral administration. Typically, it is taken once daily for a duration of 4 to 8 weeks, although longer treatment courses may be necessary in some cases. When used to treat ulcers, it should be taken after the morning meal. If prescribed as part of a combination therapy to eliminate H. pylori, it is taken twice daily, with the morning and evening meals, for a total of 7 days. It is essential to follow the instructions on your prescription label precisely. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Do not alter the dosage or frequency of rabeprazole without your doctor’s approval. Swallow the tablets whole; do not split, chew, or crush them. Rabeprazole may also be prescribed for other medical conditions. If you have questions about its use for other purposes, consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. Before starting rabeprazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to rabeprazole or other proton-pump inhibitors, such as lansoprazole (Prevacid), omeprazole (Prilosec), or pantoprazole (Protonix). Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking. Certain medications, such as cyclosporine (Neoral, Sandimmune), digoxin (Lanoxin), and ketoconazole (Nizoral), may require dose adjustments or close monitoring for potential interactions. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking rabeprazole, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking rabeprazole. If you miss a dose of rabeprazole, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is nearly time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Rabeprazole may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Headache Upset stomach Diarrhea Stomach pain Vomiting Constipation Dry mouth Changes in appetite (increased or decreased) Muscle or bone pain Drowsiness Dizziness Difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep Other side effects may occur. If you notice any unusual symptoms while taking rabeprazole, contact your doctor promptly. Store rabeprazole in its original container, ensuring it is tightly closed and kept out of reach of children. Store the medication at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal methods. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. It is important to keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor and any recommended laboratory tests. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Rabeprazole is sold under the brand name AcipHex®.
